yaml.subtitle: Quantitative methods, research design, and sociology of education
yaml.description-meta: Teaching experience of Matías Montero across Oxford and Chile.

markdown.markdown:
::: {.page-lede} My teaching spans postgraduate and undergraduate courses in quantitative methods, statistics, research design, and sociology of education. I focus on helping students connect methodological choices to meaningful substantive questions. ::: ::: {.teaching-list} ::: {.teaching-item} 2025-present ### Doctoral Teaching Fellow **Department of Education, University of Oxford** - *Introduction to Quantitative Research* - MSc and doctoral students - *Intermediate Quantitative Research* - MSc and doctoral students - Course lead: Lars-Erik Malmberg ::: ::: {.teaching-item} March 2026 ### Guest Lecturer **City St George's, University of London** - *Independent Project (MCM999)* - MA module, School of Communication & Creativity ::: ::: {.teaching-item} 2024 ### Teaching Assistant **Universidad de Chile** - *Quantitative Research Methodology in Education* - PhD in Education - *Quantitative Methodology II* - MSc in Educational Research ::: ::: {.teaching-item} 2021-2023 ### Teaching Assistant **Universidad Diego Portales** - *Basic Statistics* - MSc in Social Research Methods - *Advanced Statistical Techniques* - MSc in Social Research Methods ::: ::: {.teaching-item} 2021 ### Teaching Assistant **Universidad de Chile, Pontificia Universidad Católica de Chile, and Universidad Alberto Hurtado** - *Sociology of Education*, *Social Research Methods*, *Statistics I*, and *Mixed Methods Applied to Social Sciences* ::: ::: ## Earlier teaching Between 2017 and 2021, I supported undergraduate courses in psychological measurement, multivariate statistics, quantitative research strategies, descriptive and correlational statistics, and the social and political history of Chile and Latin America. ::: {.teaching-philosophy} ::: {.teaching-philosophy-copy}

APPROACH

## Methods are most useful when students can see the question behind them I teach quantitative work as a sequence of research decisions: defining a question, understanding the data-generating process, choosing a defensible model, and communicating uncertainty with clarity. ::: ::: {.teaching-principles}
Concept firstBuild intuition before formalism.
Applied practiceLearn by working through real research problems.
Transparent choicesMake assumptions and trade-offs visible.
::: :::
